question: what were the evaluation metrics?

evidence: Table TABREF23 shows the unlabeled INLINEFORM0 scores for our models and various baselines. All models soundly outperform right branching baselines, and we find that the neural PCFG/compound PCFG are strong models for grammar induction. In particular the compound PCFG outperforms other models by an appreciable margin on both English and Chinese. We again note that we were unable to induce meaningful grammars through a traditional PCFG with the scalar parameterization despite a thorough hyperparameter search. See lab:full for the full results (including corpus-level INLINEFORM1 ) broken down by sentence length.

title: Compound Probabilistic Context-Free Grammars for Grammar Induction
answer_short: grammaticality judgment based on sentence pairs and scores from Table TABREF23, including perplexity and syntactic evaluation
answer_rationale: The evaluation metrics include grammaticality judgment based on sentence pairs (as modified from BIBREF56 to exclude unknown words) and scores from Table TABREF23, which compare model performance against baselines. Additionally, perplexity and syntactic evaluation are mentioned as part of the evaluation, particularly in relation to PRPN/ON baselines in Table TABREF30.
